reflection.text:
After unblinding to demecolcine (PubChem CID 220401, ChEMBL CHEMBL312862, colcemid) with verdict correct: truth = Microtubule destabilizers, agent = Microtubule destabilizers, scientist call = Microtubule destabilizers p=0.71, protocol 4/4 wells at 0.1, 0.3, 1.0, 3.0 uM with similarities 0.846-0.919 (e8, unblinding tallies).

What the evidence got right:
Acquisition strategy spanning 4 doses was efficient given budget 4/4 wells (e1). e2 at 0.3 uM already gave extreme nuclear dysmorphology: nuc_form_factor z=-49.9, nuc_solidity z=-48.3, frac_large_nucleus z=+22.8 with 267 cells; e6 at 0.1 uM was even more extreme (nuc_solidity -62.8, nuc_form_factor -51.5, act_tub_ratio +17.9, 200 cells) and e7/e3 confirmed persistence at 1 uM (-46.1/-36.7) and 3 uM (-31.7/-33.0). The atlas comparison was decisive and stable: e4 2/2 Microtubule destabilizers (9/10 k-neighbours, 1/10 Eg5) and e8 4/4 Microtubule destabilizers (9/10 neighbours, summed similarity 3.596) with no Aurora neighbours, which correctly outweighed the single microscopist alternative.
Compound identity supports this: demecolcine is colcemid, a classic tubulin-targeting agent where tubulin mutations confer colcemid resistance PMID 17938271 and where colcemid/vinblastine resistance maps to microtubule-stabilizing tubulin mutations PMID 12883031.

What misled or was contradictory and why:
The microscopist description (e5: 4 fields, density lower vs DMSO, 7 observations, candidates: Aurora kinase inhibitors) was the main misleader, driven by the large, irregular nuclei phenotype noted in e2/e6/e7. I weighted this as the 0.22 Aurora hypothesis in e12 rather than dismissing it, because secondary multinucleation/polyploidy after mitotic failure can mimic Aurora in static images.
Two quantitative dose-responses also argued against a clean microtubule-destabilizer signature and justified keeping p=0.71 not higher: e10 frac_mitotic_like Spearman rho=-0.95 (p=0.051) over 4 wells/4 doses - decreasing, not increasing with dose, contrary to expected mitotic arrest; and e11 tub_mean rho=+0.80 (p=0.2) essentially flat/no loss of tubulin intensity. Review critique correctly noted these contradictions should temper confidence.
Other dose-responses were consistent: e9 nuc_form_factor rho=+1.00 (p=0) indicates dose-dependent change in shape (though sign reflects less negative at higher dose), and e14 cell_count rho=-1.00 (p=0) confirms dose-dependent cytotoxicity/proliferation block expected for an antimitotic, while e15 frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.40 (p=0.6) was flat, not supporting progressive Aurora-like polyploidy.

Which measurement/comparison/acquisition choice mattered:
The per-well NSC 1-NN vote was the anchor - unanimous across independent biological doses. The extreme negative nuc_form_factor / nuc_solidity z-scores (-31 to -62) were reproducible across e2, e3, e6, e7 and drove those atlas matches; act_tub_ratio and act_std elevations pointed away from Actin disruptors (e12). Acquiring the low 0.1 uM well (e6) was critical to show phenotype onset even at low dose, and skipping 10 uM did not hurt because 4/4 votes already saturated the protocol. No affordable well remained (budget 0/4 left) that could have altered the majority vote.

Lesson: trust the multi-dose atlas consensus when single-field human interpretation suggests Aurora based on nuclear pleiomorphism alone; retain moderate uncertainty when tubulin intensity and mitotic fraction do not show expected directionality, and plan follow-up in-cell tubulin polymerization + phospho-H3/Aurora-B assays as proposed.

This is a research screening interpretation only; no clinical advice is provided.
